findings.text: at the reviewed head the comment above LIVE_PANE_WORDS (reckon/crew/ticker.py:1059-1062) still says the held settle row 'is stale and is never released' once a later row moves the run on, but the branch it documents (reckon/crew/ticker.py:1519-1546) resolves the hold — printing it at once on a move to another live word and dropping it with a return to the shown word — so a reader is told the row merely expires, which the section's done_when forbids; commit f2bc280e1, made after the reviewed revision, rewrites the comment to state both halves, so nothing blocks landing at the worktree head, but the clause is unmet at 65c84f7fc and no test covers a comment.

assert released[-1][0]["to_state"] == "blocked" compares the released row's own field against the literal the test supplied through _row(*BLOCK); the released object is the input event passed in, so the assertion holds whatever the renderer does and survives the blank-line regression it sits beside — it identifies which row was released rather than guarding the drawing, and the real guard is the independent all(text ...) and "halted" in ... assertions at lines 104-105.

assert released[-1][0]["expected_horizon_seconds"] == 600 has the same non-independent shape as line 106: it compares a field of the input event the test handed in against the literal 600 the test itself supplied, so it cannot redden on the regression this file exists to catch, which is instead caught by the all(text ...) and "waiting" in ... assertions at lines 167 and 169.
